proposals.title: Hash function ADR and positional RNG implementation in packages/core
proposals.why_now: rand(masterSeed, namespace, ...coordinates) is the single most blocking gap in packages/core. The price generator, macro event scheduler, and bot policy engine all depend on it. ADR-002 delegates the hash function choice to a DEFINIR that must be resolved by ADR before implementation; the spec already gives a concrete starting recommendation (SplitMix64 over FNV-1a of the arguments), making the ADR decision straightforward. No downstream FASE-1 deliverable can be built until this is in place.

Branded number type Tick with constructor validator rejecting non-safe-integer and non-monotonic values

Constructor for each type rejects values outside its domain at runtime, not just at the type level
Test verifying that 1n (bigint) and 1 (number) produce distinct branded types that do not unify
proposals.title: Nominal branded types for Money, Quantity, Price, Rate, and Tick in packages/core
proposals.why_now: ADR-003 requires these types to be mechanically enforced by TypeScript; without them there is nothing preventing a Tick from being passed where a Money is expected, or a raw number from flowing through domain logic as a price. Every subsequent FASE-1 deliverable (ledger, order execution, price generator) will define its function signatures in terms of these types. Implementing them now lets the ledger and price generator be written correctly from the start rather than requiring a retrofit.

divideInt(a: number, b: number, mode: RoundingMode): number equivalent for safe-integer paths
Lint rule or type-level barrier making bare / on branded economic types a compile-time or lint-time error
Test verifying residue from truncating division equals the difference between the truncated result and exact value
proposals.title: Arithmetic helpers with explicit rounding modes and ADR-004 enforcement mechanism
proposals.why_now: ADR-004 forbids implicit division and requires every precision-losing operation to declare TRUNCATE_TOWARD_ZERO, ROUND_HALF_UP, or ROUND_HALF_EVEN. The enforcement mechanism is a DEFINIR that must be resolved by ADR before implementation; without it, division helpers exist but nothing prevents callers from using bare bigint division. Establishing this before the ledger and price generator are written avoids a retrofit across all financial calculations.

proposals.title: Minimal Electron shell with correct security configuration and CI installer artifacts
proposals.why_now: The spec contains a locked sequencing requirement: the installer exists in FASE-1, not at the end, because packaging failures (native module ABI, cross-platform path issues) discovered late are not locally correctable. FASE-1 acceptance explicitly requires a minimal installer for Windows and Linux produced by CI, and INV-29 (contextIsolation, nodeIntegration, sandbox) must be green. None of the simulation logic needs to be functional; a window that opens is sufficient and correct for this stage.

proposals.title: Double-entry multi-commodity ledger in packages/domain
proposals.why_now: The ledger is the core financial primitive that market order execution, the tick loop, and the save format all depend on. INV-04, INV-05, INV-06, and INV-07 are FASE-1 acceptance invariants that cannot be green without a working ledger. The minimum account set and transaction semantics are fully specified and unambiguous, making this implementable now that branded types and arithmetic helpers (IDEA-002, IDEA-003) establish the type foundation.

repository_assessment.current_state: Monorepo scaffold, TypeScript build system, dependency boundary enforcer, determinism lint rules, CI pipeline, and CanonicalEncoder (ADR-009) are fully implemented and tested. All other packages (world, domain, application, narrative, contracts, adapters, ui) remain empty stubs. Eight tasks completed; no active task.
repository_assessment.highest_priority_gap: packages/core is missing its positional RNG (ADR-002), which requires a hash function ADR decision first; without rand(), the price generator, macro events, and bot policies cannot be implemented, blocking all further FASE-1 simulation work.

warnings: The price generator (required for FASE-1) depends on transcendental functions (sin, exp, log for logarithmic price space) that ADR-003 prohibits as floating-point. The spec requires implementing them in fixed-point or linear-interpolation lookup tables, and states this must be documented in an ADR. No ADR exists yet for this. The price generator implementation will be blocked until this DEFINIR is resolved — the ADR should be written before or in parallel with the price generator task, not after.
